## 1. The blind and deaf, and the seeing and hearing  (`#the-blind-and-the-seeing`)

Cited ayat: 11:24

> **11:24** مَثَلُ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ كَٱلْأَعْمَىٰ وَٱلْأَصَمِّ وَٱلْبَصِيرِ وَٱلسَّمِيعِ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًا أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (11:24): The ayah says that the similitude of both groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing.

**c2** (11:24): The ayah asks whether they are equal in likeness, and asks whether they will not remember.

### One-minute summary

The ayah gives the similitude of both groups as the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing [c1]. It asks whether they are equal in likeness [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah says that the similitude of both groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing [c1]. It asks whether they are equal in likeness [c2]. It asks whether they will not remember [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah places the comparison between both groups as a pair of pairs: the blind with the deaf and the seeing with the hearing [c1]. It ends with questions, whether they are equal and whether they will not remember [c2].

### Kids mode

The ayah says that both groups are like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing [c1]. It asks whether they are equal [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture joins losing sight with losing hearing, and having sight with having hearing [c1]. Another reading is that the ayah ends with a question about remembering [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which groups are meant in this ayah; it says both groups, and the ayat that say which are outside the ayah cited here.
- Not established: which group is likened to which half of the picture; this draft keeps the ayah's own wording.
- The ayah itself uses the word for a similitude (mathal).
